# Editor Scope

## How To Build

A EditorScope should be built as a reusable component that will be reused throughout the rest of the codebase.  A component is configurable through arguments or properties that alter its behaviour, appearance, and details.  A EditorScope should encapsulate all of its own reusable behaviour, while leaving the wiring, intergration, and integration to the domain of the application.

## Theme

Drawn in the [ThemeScope](../../ui/theme/index.md#theme-scope): its surfaces, text, lines, accent, and status colours are the theme's roles, named as the theme names them, in both dark and light mode, never colours of its own.

## Concept

### Pitch

An editor for a file opened from the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope), or anywhere else the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, with language support for Piton files.

### Shape

#### Description

Editable and syntax highlighted, under a header with the file's path in the project, a dot while it has unsaved changes, a save button, and a close button.

#### Syntax Highlighting

Every file is highlighted in its language, using the grammars gpui-kit's editor comes with: Piton, and Astro, Bash, C, C++, C#, CMake, CSS, diffs, EJS, Elixir, ERB, Go, GraphQL, HTML, Java, JavaScript, JSON, Kotlin, Lua, Make, Markdown, PHP, Protocol Buffers, Python, Ruby, Rust, Scala, Svelte, Swift, TOML, TSX, TypeScript, YAML, and Zig. SQL is left out, as its grammar can't be built alongside gpui.
The language comes from the file's extension, ignoring case, including the other extensions a language goes by, such as .h for C, .hpp and .cc for C++, .jsx, .mjs, and .cjs for JavaScript, .mts and .cts for TypeScript, .htm for HTML, .exs for Elixir, .zsh for Bash, .yml for YAML, and .scss, .sass, and .less for CSS. Some files are known by their whole name instead: Makefile for Make, CMakeLists.txt for CMake, Cargo.lock for TOML, Gemfile and Rakefile for Ruby, and shell startup files like .bashrc and .zshrc for Bash. A file in any other language, or with no extension, is plain text.

#### Selecting Text

Selecting text in the editor by dragging across it shows a [SelectionPopoverScope](../../ui/components/selection-popover/index.md#selection-popover-scope) with four buttons:

- Cut, with a scissors icon, which puts the selected text on the clipboard and removes it from the file
- Copy, with a copy icon, which puts the selected text on the clipboard
- Paste, with a clipboard icon, which puts what is on the clipboard in place of the selected text
- Send to Prompt, with a paperclip icon, which attaches the selected text to the prompt, as attaching text selected in an answer does

Cut, Copy, and Paste do just what their shortcuts do in the editor, and can be undone the same way. Cut and Paste are disabled while the file can't be edited yet. After any of them the editor keeps focus. The popover also closes when the text changes, or when the file closes.

#### Ruler

A thin vertical line, in the theme's line colour, runs down the text at the 80th column, the width a line should keep within. Past it, the editor's background is a step darker than the well, as black laid over it, 25% in dark mode and 5% in light mode, so text running long stands out while staying as readable. The line and the shade scroll sideways with the text, are drawn behind it, and never take the mouse.

#### Keyboard

##### Indentation

A tab stop is 4 spaces: <Tab> indents by 4 spaces, <Shift+Tab> outdents by 4, and a new line's indentation counts in 4s.

##### Backspace

<Backspace> with nothing selected, when everything between the start of the line and the cursor is spaces, deletes back to the tab stop before the cursor, up to 4 spaces at once, as though the indentation were tabs. Anywhere else, or with a selection, it deletes as ever, a character or the selection.

##### Home

The editor moves about a line the way a good code editor does. <Home> goes to the line's first character that isn't whitespace; pressed again there, or on a line that is only whitespace, it goes to the very start of the line, and pressed again from there, back to its first character. With <Shift> it selects the same way.

##### New Lines

<Enter> starts the new line at the indentation of the line it breaks, as the language's indentation rules say. On a line that is an item of a Markdown or Piton list, starting with a dash, an asterisk, or a plus and a space, or a number and a period and a space, the new line starts a new item of the same list at the same indentation, a numbered item counting on from the one before. <Enter> on an item with nothing after its marker ends the list

###### Instead

the marker is taken away, leaving the line empty at its

indentation. <Enter> with an open completion or quick fix menu is the menu's.

#### New Files

The editor can also show a file that isn't on disk yet, starting with the text it is given. It has unsaved changes from the start, and saving it writes it, making its folders as needed.

#### Saving

Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on macOS) or the save button writes the file to disk. A file that cannot be saved keeps its changes and says why beneath the header.
Saving never moves the cursor or the view. A Piton file is formatted as it is saved, and the editor then shows the formatted text, with the cursor still at the same place in the text, beside the same characters it was beside, and scrolled just as it was.

#### Language Support

```
overview: A Piton file (`.pi`) is edited with the project's [LSP](../lsp/index.md#lsp) server, shared with the chat input, which sees the editor's unsaved text: the file is opened with `textDocument/didOpen`, kept current with full-text `textDocument/didChange`, reported with `textDocument/didSave` when saved, and closed with `textDocument/didClose` when the editor closes or shows another file. Other files are edited without language support, as is a Piton file while the server is not running.
completions: `textDocument/completion` is requested after typing a letter, a digit, an opening curly brace, a period, a dollar sign, an at sign, a colon, or an underscore, and narrowed and ordered as in the chat input. Accepting a completion also applies the import the server attaches to it.
## Concept

### Pitch

The main window's body: the area to the right of the project sidebar, where the tasks sent to the harness, and any file opened beside them, are shown, and the chat input they are sent from.

### Shape

#### Description

Beneath the [RibbonScope](../../ui/components/ribbon/index.md#ribbon-scope), to the right of the [ProjectSidebarScope](../../ui/components/project-sidebar/index.md#project-sidebar-scope), which runs the full height beside it, and reaching the window's right edge. It is part of the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor).
The [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) lives within the body, along its bottom: its left edge against the project sidebar, and the message list above it. While a task runs, the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](../../ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/index.md#referenced-spec-sidebar-scope) runs the body's full height at its right, beside both the message list and the chat input, and the chat input's right edge is against it: the chat input never runs beneath the right sidebar. While that sidebar isn't there, the chat input reaches the window's right edge.

#### Contents

Everything that can be in the body:

- the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list), the chat history, which fills the space above the chat input whenever no file is open
- the hint shown in the message list's place before any task has been sent, or while no project is open, as the [PromptEditor](../prompt-mode/index.md#prompt-editor) and the [NoProjectStateScope](../no-project/index.md#no-project-state-scope) say
- an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope), in a split beside the message list, while a file is open
- the [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope), along the bottom beneath the message list and any file open beside it
- the [ReferencedSpecSidebarScope](../../ui/components/referenced-spec-sidebar/index.md#referenced-spec-sidebar-scope), at the right of all of these, the chat input included, while a task runs

An [InsetPanelScope](../../ui/components/inset-panel/index.md#inset-panel-scope) floats over the whole window, the body included, but is never part of it.

#### Open File

A file opened, from the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope) or anywhere else the [OpenFileScope](../open-file/index.md#open-file-scope) says, shows in an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope), in a split beside the chat history: the file on the left taking 50% of the width, the chat history on the right taking the rest. The split can be resized by dragging its edge. Closing the file closes the split.
When the split opens, it slides in from the sidebar, so it's clear where it came from: the file's side grows out of the sidebar's edge to its share of the width, the file sliding into view from behind that edge as it does, over the chat history. The chat history keeps its width while the file slides over it, so nothing in it is laid out anew each frame, and takes the rest of the width once the slide settles.
The slide is quick and settles without bouncing, and only then can the split be dragged. A file opened in place of one already showing doesn't slide, since the split is already open. The [ChatInputScope](../prompt-mode/chat-input/index.md#chat-input-scope) is never split: it stays along the bottom, beneath both the file and the chat history.
Closing the file plays the slide in reverse, back into the

##### Sidebar

the file's side shrinks from whatever width it was

dragged to down to nothing at the sidebar's edge, the file sliding out of view behind that edge as it does, uncovering the chat history, which is back across the full width beneath it from the start of the slide. It is as quick as the slide in, and settles without bouncing. Opening a file while one is still sliding out slides the new one in straight away.

## Concept

### Pitch

Opens one of the project's files to read or edit, from wherever the file is named, always in the same place.

### Shape

#### Description

A file opens in an [EditorScope](../editor/index.md#editor-scope), in the split beside the chat history that the [BodyScope](../application/Body.md#body-scope) lays out. Opening a file while another is showing shows it in that one's place, the editor first asking to discard any unsaved changes.

#### Opened From

A file opens this way, however it is opened:

- clicking it in the [FileTreeScope](../../ui/components/file-tree/index.md#file-tree-scope)
- picking it in the [PaletteScope](../palette/index.md#palette-scope), or its search for a file finding just that one, which closes the palette
- clicking a link to it in a task's compiled prompt or reply text, or its path on a row of the [MessageList](../prompt-mode/message-list/index.md#message-list)
- the button for opening it in a [DiffViewScope](../../ui/components/diff-view/index.md#diff-view-scope)'s header, which closes the diff first
- going to a definition in another file from the editor, which opens that file at the definition

#### Missing

A link to a file that doesn't exist shows an error notification, and opens nothing.

I haven't changed any code yet, because the spec still describes the slide-out and I'd have to invent most of the tab design:
- **`Body.pi`** says a file opens in a split beside the chat history at 50% width, sliding in from the sidebar and back out when closed.
- **`open-file/index.pi`** says one file at a time: opening another replaces it, after asking about unsaved changes.
- **`editor/index.pi`** gives the editor its own header with path, unsaved dot, save and close buttons.

This session runs in code mode, so I can't update the spec myself. If I built tabs without it, the next build from the spec would put the slide-out back.

These are the gaps I'd otherwise be filling in myself, each with what I'd suggest:
1. **Where the tab bar sits.** Along the top of the body, above the message list, left of the referenced spec sidebar.
2. **Whether the chat history is a tab.** Yes, a fixed first tab (say "Chat") that can't be closed, so the body shows one thing at a time.
3. **The chat input.** It stays along the bottom whichever tab is selected, so you can prompt while looking at a file.
4. **Tab look.** gpui-kit's default tabs, each showing the file name, an unsaved-changes dot and a close button. The full path goes in a tooltip and in the editor's header.
5. **Opening a file that's already open.** It selects that tab instead of opening a second one. A new file gets a new tab after the selected one, and is selected.
6. **Closing a tab with unsaved changes.** It asks first, as replacing a file does now, then selects the neighbouring tab (or Chat).
7. **The slide animation.** It goes entirely, including the split and its drag edge.
8. **Tabs across projects.** Switching projects closes that project's file tabs, as the open file does today, unless you want them kept per project.
